findings.example: 3 دن پہلے اپ ڈیٹ کیا گیا
findings.problem: Source-order calque: the age follows the passive verb, composed as 'اپ ڈیٹ کیا گیا 3 دن پہلے'. Urdu fronts a relative-time phrase ('3 دن پہلے اپ ڈیٹ کیا گیا'). This key is one whole message precisely so the language can reorder it: the sidecar says the time may go before the verb, and the org-teams-list call-site comment names the shipped 'updated 2 دن پہلے' order as the defect the whole-message change removes. Measured with fribidi (RTL base), the age occupies the leftmost 9 columns - the end a single-line ellipsis truncates first. Shipped ui.settings.integrations...worked_when_with_tools renders 'Worked {when}' as '{when} کام کیا', the same time-first shape proposed here. Counter-evidence weighed: shipped ui.hub.teams.detail.created/updated and ui.agents.config.summary.updated use the same post-verbal shape, so this is not a term clash; but those placeholders are a formatted date or a name in label/value rows, while these three are whole single-line sentences the sidecar and call site explicitly freed for reordering.

observations.detail: With a Latin {name} that starts or ends with punctuation, the Unicode bidi algorithm moves that punctuation to the other end of the name inside these RTL paragraphs: measured fribidi RTL visuals '!Beta' -> 'Beta!' and 'Really?' -> '?Really' (both in ui.agents.config.placeholder.about and in the publish titles). The catalogue value is correct and manual bidi controls are forbidden (ur-activation.test.mjs), so this is not a copy defect: {name} is user data and the render layer does not isolate it. This is shared by existing shipped keys that embed {name}. The fix, if wanted, is call-site isolation (FSI/PDI around the placeholder) exactly as hub-skills-library.tsx does for a local path; it is outside this catalogue audit and does not gate these 25 values.

observations.topic: bidi: 'Agent Hub' Latin run and the کیا … ؟ question
observations.detail: Measured with fribidi RTL: U+061F ARABIC QUESTION MARK is bidi class AL, so it always lands at the visual left end of the RTL line (log39 -> vis0 with 'AcmeBot', log40 -> vis0 with '3D-Forge'), i.e. the correct end. The Latin run 'Agent Hub' stays intact and in place between its Urdu neighbours, and the quotes bracket the name correctly for RTL reading: U+201C sits immediately to the right of the name (vis35 vs name vis28..34) and U+201D immediately to its left (vis27). No leading punctuation displacement is measured under the app's RTL base direction; the receipt titles that begin with “ plus a Latin name still start at the right (U+201C log0 -> vis41 of 42).

terminology_rulings.item: Ask for X: مانگیں vs shipped طلب کریں
terminology_rulings.basis: The locale already splits the two actions this way: asking for a new agent/team is مانگیں (ui.agents.pages.empty.agents/teams 'نیچے سے ایک مانگیں'), while requesting a change is طلب کریں (ui.agents.config.composer.label '… تبدیلی طلب کریں', ui.agents.detail.action.ask_change). طلب کریں in this heading would collide with the change-request verb; مانگیں is the shipped call for this action and a polite imperative, consistent with آپ.

Noun (delegation), consistent with ui.agents.detail.delegate.label 'ذیلی ایجنٹس کو تفویض کر سکتا ہے' and ui.agents.upload.list.surface '… اور تفویض …'. It states the capability as a noun (the sidecar forbids a verb) and does not duplicate the switch's editable sentence.

حاصل کرنا is the shipped verb for obtaining (ui.agents.dialogs.create.hub_link '… حاصل کرنے کے لیے Agent Hub دیکھیں'; ui.agents.detail.alert.builtin_body). It also keeps the visible label distinct from the button's accessible name 'Download {name}' (ڈاؤن لوڈ), which is the English pair's own distinction.

Byte-identical to the shipped ui.hub.teams.public.trying 'Trying…', and the same '… جاری ہے…' in-flight shape as ui.agents.navigation.updates.action.retrying 'دوبارہ کوشش جاری ہے…'; the retry action itself stays دوبارہ کوشش کریں.

terminology_rulings.item: Publish question shape: کیا “{name}” کو … شائع کریں؟
terminology_rulings.basis: 'کیا … کریں؟' is the standard Urdu confirmation-question frame (interrogative + subjunctive) and ends with U+061F ؟. The name is quoted with the locale's “ ” (the source quotes it too) and the destination is named; the organisation uses میں (publish in the organisation) while the public target uses Agent Hub پر (on the hub), so the two destinations do not read as the same place.
